channel.title: Personal News Feed — News & World Affairs
channel.description: Personally scored news, world affairs, opinion/analysis & foreign affairs, business & finance, and San Diego/local articles curated by news-filter

item.title: German Chancellor Merz Calls for Korean Reunification at DMZ
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: Germany news: Merz hopes for Korean reunification at DMZ
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited the demilitarized zone (DMZ) between North and South Korea, expressing hope for Korean reunification akin to Germany's 1990 unification. At the Panmunjom truce village, Merz emphasized the pain of division and the desire for reunification, referencing Germany's experience. North Korea, however, has distanced itself from reunification talks, removing such language from its constitution and labeling South Korea a 'hostile state.' Meanwhile, Germany's inflation rate dropped to 2.8% in October, driven by a fuel tax cut, though rising energy prices could offset savings. President Frank-Walter Steinmeier's recent trip to China aimed to balance diplomatic respect with criticism over trade issues, with Chinese President Xi Jinping pledging to advance the 'comprehensive strategic partnership.' Other news included vandalism of a Manchester United memorial in Munich and Audi's sharp profit decline. Merz's remarks underscore Berlin's cautious approach to regional stability, while economic and diplomatic developments highlight Germany's multifaceted challenges.

item.title: Scientists Discover X-Ray Sources, Link Movement to Learning, and Amygdala's Role in Memory
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: Science Original headline: This week in science: mysterious X-rays, movement and learning, and memory formation
Scientists discovered three key findings in recent research. A study by Luke Rosedahl, published in Science Advances, found that large physical movements, like swinging a lightsaber, significantly enhance category learning compared to button presses. Participants in VR games learned to categorize striped objects up to six times faster with bigger motions. Researchers suggest this could improve training for tasks like sorting medical images. Another study, led by Ueli Rutishauser at Cedars-Sinai, revealed the amygdala plays a critical role in forming long-term visual memories. By monitoring brain activity in epilepsy patients, they found that active amygdala neurons correlated with better memory retention. Denise Cai noted this is the first evidence of the amygdala as a memory control center in humans. Lastly, astronomers Jimmy Irwin and Mustafa Muhibullah identified 84 new low-energy X-ray sources in distant galaxies, possibly linked to black holes siphoning material from stars. These findings could help measure the universe's expansion rate. The research was published in Nature Astronomy and Nature Neuroscience.

item.title: UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara to expire amid US, Russia vetoes
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle
The United Nations peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara, MINURSO, will expire as Russia and the United States vetoed each other's draft resolutions to extend its mandate. Established in 1991 to oversee a ceasefire between Morocco and the Polisario Front, the mission faces expiration after a failed attempt to renew it. The U.S. proposed a one-year extension, replacing MINURSO with MINUSO and making Morocco's autonomy plan the sole basis for negotiations. Russia opposed this as a 'unilateral approach,' blocking the resolution. The U.S. later vetoed a Russian draft that preserved the original terms. Morocco welcomed the mission's end, while the Polisario Front thanked Russia for blocking the U.S. proposal, which they claimed would undermine Sahrawi self-determination. The Security Council's inability to resolve the decades-old dispute persists.

item.title: Oceanside Prepares for Weekend Rain Amid El Niño
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Oceanside discusses planning & preparing for weekend weather amid El Niño
Oceanside officials are preparing for heavy rain and rising sea levels expected this weekend due to El Niño. Assistant City Manager Michael Grossman said the city anticipates significant rainfall and rapid water rise in low-lying areas like Buena Vista lagoon and creeks. He noted lift stations, which pump wastewater to sewer plants, are vulnerable to backups. Last week, the city declared a state of emergency to expedite resource procurement for El Niño preparedness. Grossman emphasized that prior planning helped streamline response efforts, ensuring staff know their roles and responsibilities for the storm. The city has already implemented measures to protect residents and infrastructure ahead of the weather event.

item.title: Patrick Stewart died from rapid dementia progression
item.description:
Source: Washington Post Original headline: Patrick Stewart died after a ‘brief’ journey with dementia. Is that common?
Patrick Stewart died from rapid dementia progression, experts say. The actor, known for his role as Captain Jean-Luc Picard, passed away after a brief illness linked to Lewy Body Dementia and Alzheimer’s. Medical experts note that rapidly progressive dementia, which occurs within less than two years, is rare, affecting less than 5% of all dementia cases. Lewy Body Dementia accounts for 10-20% of these cases. Symptoms include cognitive fluctuations, visual hallucinations, and sleep disturbances. Robin Williams, who struggled with Lewy Body Dementia, died by suicide, highlighting the disease’s severity. Early stages may not show symptoms, but as the disease advances, it can progress rapidly. Proper diagnosis is critical, as misdiagnosis can lead to harmful treatments. Experts emphasize the need for a multidisciplinary approach, including therapy and support groups, to manage the condition. While the exact causes of Lewy Body Dementia remain unclear, it often coexists with Parkinson’s and Alzheimer’s, complicating treatment. Early detection and tailored care are essential to improve quality of life for patients and their families.

item.title: Chesapeake Oyster Stocks Plummet; Resident Aims to Restore
item.description:
Source: NPR Topics: News Original headline: Oyster stocks have plunged in the Chesapeake. This resident wants to bring them back
Oyster stocks in the Chesapeake Bay have declined by over 99% since 2011 due to overharvesting, leading to poorer water quality and reduced habitats. John Consoli, a Maryland resident and University of Maryland photographer, is working to restore oyster populations by farming them and promoting conservation. Oysters filter up to 50 gallons of water daily, improving water quality and supporting marine life. Consoli floats oysters in nutrient-rich zones to aid growth, though challenges like murky waters complicate planting and harvesting. Biologist Ryan Carnegie notes recent gains from better management, but populations remain below historical levels. Miao Yu, a mechanical engineer, is developing robots like Oysterbot and BlueROV to map oyster habitats using sonar and AI, aiming to provide farmers with precise data for planting and harvesting. Consoli also collaborates with neighbors and a local restaurant, Libbey's Coastal Kitchen, to deploy a million baby oysters. His efforts, dubbed the 'Peer to Pier Network,' aim to rebuild oyster reefs and restore the bay's ecosystem. 'It teaches me how something so insignificant can make a difference,' Consoli says, highlighting the role of community and technology in conservation.

item.title: Rising Fuel Prices Drive Up Holiday Travel Costs, Airlines Raise Fares
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: As war-driven fuel prices drive up cost of travel, will it matter during the holidays?
Rising fuel prices are driving up holiday travel costs, with gasoline averaging $4.27 per gallon and airfares climbing due to soaring jet fuel expenses. Airlines like JetBlue and Frontier have raised fares to offset rising fuel costs, with JetBlue’s fuel price up 57% year-over-year. AAA spokesperson Mark Jenkins noted that while higher fuel prices influence travel decisions, driving remains the dominant mode for holidays, as families often find it more economical than flying. Crude oil prices exceeding $100 per barrel and disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have kept gas prices elevated despite seasonal declines. Analysts warn that airfares will stay high, with JetBlue’s average fare now higher than major carriers. Discount airlines like Frontier and Allegiant also face pressure, with Frontier raising fares 71% in a money-losing quarter. Amtrak reported increased ridership during last year’s government shutdown but offers limited discounts for holiday travel. Fuel costs continue to shape travel choices, though consumers have adapted by combining trips or driving less.

item.title: Encinitas Implements Temporary Rent Caps for Mobile Home Parks
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: Encinitas enacts mobile home park rent control on an immediate, temporary basis
Encinitas City Council approved temporary rent control for mobile home parks, effective immediately. The measure caps annual rent increases at 4% or 75% of the San Diego CPI, whichever is lower. Council members cited the need to address rising costs for low-income residents, noting mobile home park residents often face limited relocation options. The decision followed pressure from residents of Riviera Mobile Home Park, who faced potential 17% rate hikes. A second temporary ordinance, set to expire in 2027, will require a November vote and 30-day waiting period. Council members emphasized the need for a permanent solution by then. Some stakeholders, including a park owner and industry representatives, expressed concerns about regulatory burdens and called for careful consideration of varying park conditions. The urgency ordinance requires a supermajority vote and allows park owners to petition for higher rates if they deem the caps unfair.

item.title: Helicopter crash kills six pilgrims in Uttarakhand
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Six dead after helicopter crashes in northern Indian state
A helicopter carrying five pilgrims and a pilot crashed in Uttarakhand's Chamoli district, killing six people. The aircraft departed from Badrinath, a Char Dham pilgrimage site, on Friday afternoon before losing contact. Heavy rain and poor visibility were reported in the area. Uttarakhand's Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami confirmed the crash site near a village close to Joshimath. The local civil aviation authority later identified six bodies. Helicopter services, popular for pilgrims avoiding mountain treks, face safety concerns after multiple accidents. A 2025 crash near Kedarnath killed seven, and another in October 2022 claimed seven lives. During the 2025 pilgrimage season, several other accidents prompted aviation authorities to tighten safety checks and restrict operations. The crash comes amid an orange weather alert for thunderstorms, hail, and strong winds in the region.

item.title: San Diego Luxury Real Estate Market Slows Amid Market Uncertainty
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: San Diego’s luxury real estate market was on fire this summer. Not anymore
San Diego’s luxury real estate market has cooled after a summer surge. Pending sales for homes over $2 million dropped to 120 in October from 232 in May, according to Reports on Housing. Sales times for high-end properties increased significantly, with homes priced $2 million to $4 million taking an average of 172 days to sell in October, up from 87 days in May. Steven Thomas of Reports on Housing noted wealthy buyers are concerned about stock market volatility, particularly the Nasdaq, and rising interest rates. Higher borrowing costs are deterring some business owners from investing, including luxury home purchases. Venture capital in San Diego has declined, with $804 million raised in Q2, down from $3.16 billion in Q1 2021. The Sand Castle mansion, listed at $87.5 million since May 2024, remains on the market. Reports on Housing attributes the slowdown to broader economic factors rather than elections, as high-income tax proposals have minimal impact on the housing market.

item.title: US approves sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
item.description:
Source: BBC News
The United States has approved the sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine, valued at $2.1bn, to bolster its defense against Russian aerial attacks. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned deliveries could take 'several years' due to global shortages and production delays. The State Department stated Ukraine will fund the purchase through donations from Canada, Germany, Norway, and EU support via the JUMPSTART program. Lockheed Martin will manufacture the missiles, with no U.S. taxpayer funds involved. Zelensky criticized the U.S. for slow approval, emphasizing urgent needs as Russia intensifies attacks on Ukraine's energy infrastructure. The sale aims to enhance European security, per U.S. foreign policy goals. Tensions persist over Russia's presence at the G20, where European diplomats protested its participation. Zelensky highlighted critical shortages, noting Ukraine has awaited missile supplies for nearly a month.

item.title: Asana CEO uses AI agents for inbox, calendar, and competitor tracking
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Asana's CEO lets AI agents manage his inbox, monitor performance, and track rivals
Asana's CEO Dan Rogers uses AI agents to manage his inbox, calendar, customer relationships, and competitor tracking. The company expanded its AI collaboration tools in 2024, allowing users to interact with AI agents for work tasks. Rogers, who became CEO in 2023, relies on bots to prioritize emails, monitor time allocation, and flag new commitments. He emphasized that work-oriented agents differ from consumer tools by understanding organizational knowledge and handling sensitive data. Some agents required refinement, like a competitor-tracking bot that initially flagged irrelevant info until instructed otherwise. Rogers checks in weekly with a customer-monitoring agent to address concerns proactively. Another agent answers employee product questions by drawing on internal resources. A performance-tracking agent provides sales and customer metrics without needing human intervention, while a rival-monitoring agent compares features with Asana's offerings. Rogers also uses an engineering capacity agent to allocate resources efficiently. He stressed security measures, restricting data access for sensitive tasks. Agents communicate independently without his oversight, streamlining decision-making.

item.title: NTSB Details Water Bucket Issues in Yosemite Helicopter Crash
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: NTSB releases new details of deadly Yosemite National Park firefighter helicopter crash
A firefighting helicopter crashed in Yosemite National Park on Sept. 20 while battling the Dome fire, killing pilots Greg King and Ryan Cutter. A preliminary NTSB report states the aircraft had issues with its 800-gallon water bucket earlier that day during 25 water drops. Mechanics tightened the bucket’s air pressure regulator and performed a pressure check before the pilots were asked to conduct three more drops. The crash occurred during the third drop at Ostrander Lake around 1:56 p.m. Flight data and firefighter videos show the bucket swung left, the helicopter rapidly descended, and the bucket struck the ground. The 200-foot cable detached, and the helicopter crashed into trees, coming to rest on its left side. Most of the aircraft was consumed by fire post-crash, limiting data recovery. The NTSB continues its investigation. The Dome fire burned over 6,700 acres after being ignited by an abandoned campfire near Yosemite’s southern entrance on Sept. 15.

item.title: High Tides Damage 114 Structures in Huntington Beach
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: High tides damage 114 structures in Huntington Beach. City warns of more flooding to come
High tides and flooding damaged 114 homes and structures in Huntington Beach, including six yellow-tagged homes and a fire caused by saltwater damaging a lithium-ion battery. King tides flooded parts of Pacific Coast Highway, forcing road closures. The city declared a state of emergency, deploying emergency services and activating a command post. Officials warn late-November tides could be higher, increasing flood risks. Experts link the event to potential El Niño storms, prompting cities to use sandbags, pumps, and drainage systems for preparation. City officials urge residents in low-lying areas to assess properties, secure sandbags, and review emergency plans. Tides have already caused significant damage, with officials emphasizing ongoing threats despite water receding.

item.title: Second Scripps Park Picnic Grove Opens After Years of Delays
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: ‘Absolutely awesome’: Second picnic grove, years in the making, now open at Scripps Park
The second Scripps Park picnic grove opened to the public on Oct. 23 after nearly four years of planning and permit delays. The project, inspired by the first grove opened in December 2022, includes the same GraniteCrete paving, relocated tables, and a new barbecue. Construction began Sept. 14, but delays stemmed from securing a right-of-entry permit from the city of San Diego. Volunteers initiated the permit process in January 2024, with the permit signed in January 2025 for a one-year term. Funding challenges arose as initial donors covered only 50% of costs, prompting Corsi to seek a $10,000 grant from the Kiwanis Club of La Jolla and additional funds from La Jolla Parks & Beaches. A new city planner later complicated the permit extension process, requiring Corsi and volunteers to re-establish timelines. Corsi praised the space as 'absolutely awesome,' thanking donors including Brian Malk, Ann Lipschitz, Ann Dynes, Tim Seery, the Kiwanis Club, and contractors Jim Neri and Alan Cronin for their support.

item.title: Encore Sushi Opens in Cedros Design District
item.description:
Source: San Diego Reader stories Original headline: West and La bring Encore Sushi to Cedros
Chef James La and business partner Chris West have reopened the Cedros Avenue restaurant space as Encore Sushi. The location previously housed Local Roots Kombucha and Kai Ola Sushi, which closed its Solana Beach location in June. Encore celebrated its grand opening October 23, offering upscale casual sushi with a musical theme. West noted the previous concept didn't fit the Cedros Design District crowd, describing the new venture as providing 'a night out' experience. The menu includes sections like 'Opening Act' and 'Greatest Hits,' with rolls named Crowd Surfer and Ring of Fire. The space is adjacent to Belly Up, influencing the venue's musical branding. Other recent additions to the neighborhood include Rare Society and Vále Bodega. Encore operates Tuesday through Sunday, featuring a $5 happy hour from 3 to 5:30 pm. La, a sushi veteran, sees this as a return to the area rather than a new start.

item.title: Proton CTO outlines AI's impact on coding roles, engineers react
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Proton's CTO wrote a manifesto for the AI coding age. It struck a nerve with engineers.
Proton CTO Bart Butler released a manifesto arguing that software engineers' roles are being redefined by AI. The three-page memo claims engineers must shift from writing code to guiding large language models (LLMs) in generating better code. Butler stated, 'Your job is to help the LLM write better code faster,' rejecting the idea that AI tools like LLMs assist in writing code. Proton previously admitted to being 'too blunt' in communicating this shift. Engineers reacted strongly, with OpenAI's Peter Steinberger calling the memo 'dead on,' predicting the 'old job of software engineer is gone' if AI progress continues. David Heinemeier Hansson warned employees unprepared for the change would face challenges. Lauren Tan of SpaceX echoed the memo's message, stating engineers now lead model teams. Plover Labs' Edward Ahn noted Proton's memo was among the most candid from CEOs about AI's impact. The memo has sparked widespread discussion about the future of coding roles in an AI-driven era.

item.title: Mortgage Rates Drop to 7.18% Today
item.description:
Source: NerdWallet Original headline: Mortgage Rates Today, Friday, October 30: Noticeably Lower
Mortgage rates dropped to 7.18% APR today, down 14 basis points from yesterday and 2 basis points from a week ago. The average 30-year rate for October was 7.3%, higher than September's 6.98%. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh noted September's rate hike is "starting to work some" on reducing inflation, though price stability hasn't been achieved. The October PCE report, due November 25, will show the rate hike's impact. The October jobs report on November 6 could influence potential December rate decisions. Refinancing may be worthwhile if current rates are 0.5-0.75% lower than existing rates, though most borrowers aren't eligible. Lenders adjust rates daily, so locking in a rate is advised if a deal is satisfactory. Rates are unlikely to change significantly until Monday.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Tips to Make $50 Holiday Gifts Feel Worth $100
item.description:
Source: NerdWallet Original headline: How to Make a $50 Holiday Gift Feel Like $100
NerdWallet suggests strategies to make $50 holiday gifts feel like $100. The author shares methods to elevate inexpensive gifts, such as using niche gift cards tailored to recipients' interests, engraving items with names, and creating custom experiences. Examples include transforming family photos into themed artwork, crafting personalized frames with recipient photos, and making homemade treats in decorative tins. Experiential gifts like museum memberships or charity donations are also highlighted, offering shared activities and community engagement. The author emphasizes personalization over cost, noting that thoughtful customization adds perceived value without significant expense. Tips include leveraging online tutorials for crafting, using existing social media photos for gifts, and combining purchased items with DIY touches. The goal is to create meaningful, memorable gifts within a budget, fostering connection without overspending.

item.title: European diplomats avoid Russia at G20 meeting in Atlanta
item.description:
Source: Deutsche Welle Original headline: European diplomats shun Russia at G20 gathering in the US
European diplomats refused to take a photo with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta, hosted by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. Germany's Johann Wadephul cited no normalcy with Russia, while the two-day gathering precedes a December G20 leaders summit in Miami hosted by Donald Trump. Discussions focused on global crises, including energy and trade disruptions, but tensions persist over Ukraine, with Russia willing to meet Zelenskyy in Moscow if he travels there. Lavrov denied easing ties with the US, calling the diesel deal 'no illusions.' EU diplomat Kaja Kallas criticized Lavrov's 'lies' about Ukraine, while British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband urged action for peace. South Africa, a G20 founding member, was excluded from the meeting, with officials calling the nonparticipation 'not voluntary.' The meeting is expected to end with a US-drafted summary instead of a joint declaration.

item.title: Vessel overturns near Del Mar Jetty, one dies
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: 1 dead after vessel overturned near Del Mar Jetty
A vessel overturned near the Del Mar Jetty Friday evening, killing one person and injuring another. Oceanside Fire Department responders arrived at 6:57 p.m. after a 911 call from someone on the vessel. The caller reported a person was missing in the water. Authorities conducted a search and rescue, locating the missing individual at 7:31 p.m. near where the boat struck rocks and capsized. The deceased was transported to the hospital and pronounced dead, while the second victim received minor injuries. The incident's cause is under investigation. This is a developing story.

item.title: New Rainstorm Approaches L.A. for Halloween, Forecasters Warn of Light Showers
item.description:
Source: LA Times Original headline: A new rainstorm moves in Friday. What does it means for L.A. Halloween?
A new rainstorm is expected to arrive in Los Angeles on Friday, impacting Halloween weather. The National Weather Service forecasts stray showers and temperatures 5 to 10 degrees below normal. The storm system is projected to peak Saturday evening into Sunday morning with a 70% chance of rain. Ryan Kittell, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service, estimates rainfall between 0.5 to 1 inch. He advises planning for rain during Halloween activities but notes the precipitation is likely light. The last recorded Halloween rainfall in L.A. was 0.25 inches in 2014. Forecasters predict minimal impacts, including potential traffic delays and minor roadway flooding, with the primary effect being on Halloween events.

item.title: DEA approves medical marijuana dispensary registrations for tax benefits
item.description:
Source: San Diego Union-Tribune Original headline: DEA approvals could bring big tax benefits for medical marijuana businesses
The U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration has approved registrations for over 900 state-licensed medical marijuana dispensaries in Alabama, Florida, Mississippi, South Dakota, Texas, Virginia, and West Virginia. This follows President Trump’s rescheduling of marijuana to Schedule III, which allows businesses to access federal tax benefits previously denied due to Schedule I classification. Attorney General Todd Blanche stated the move ensures broader access to chronic pain treatment and public safety. Nearly 7,000 cannabis businesses have applied for registration. Steph Sherer of Americans for Safe Access called the approvals a victory for patient access, marking the first federal recognition of medical cannabis dispensaries. However, uncertainties remain about DEA regulations, as state oversight differs from Schedule III standards. Some states permit individuals with criminal records to operate marijuana businesses, but it’s unclear if the DEA will adopt similar leniency. Chris Lindsey of the American Trade Association for Cannabis and Hemp noted the focus is on what requirements the DEA will impose on registered companies. The decision legitimizes medical marijuana programs in 40 states, though recreational and medical industries in some states may face unclear regulatory paths.

item.title: Ukrainian Ceasefire Facilitates Oleshky Evacuation Amid Humanitarian Aid
item.description:
Source: BBC News, Deutsche Welle Original headline: Ukraine Ceasefire Enables Evacuation of Oleshky Residents Amid Humanitarian Efforts
Residents of Oleshky, a Russian-occupied city in Ukraine's Kherson region, evacuated under a humanitarian ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. Up to 750 people left the area on Friday, transported via buses to Belarus and then to Ukraine's Chernihiv region. The operation, part of the longest and most widespread truce since Russia's 2022 invasion, included a four-hour departure window ending at 14:00 local time. Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets and Russia's Yana Lantratova coordinated the evacuation during a joint visit to Oleshky, with Lubinets emphasizing the humanitarian focus. Deutsche Welle reported demining operations resulted in two deaths, including a Russian sapper. Pope Francis and Trump facilitated the ceasefire and evacuation efforts. Residents faced dire conditions, with many lacking electricity and water. Olena, a Kyiv resident, explained her family stayed in Oleshky due to challenges like transporting animals and elderly reluctance, citing a relative's death from a landmine last winter. Evacuees were offered relocation options to Ukrainian-held areas, Russian-controlled territories, or to remain with aid. The operation continues through Sunday evening.

item.title: Hospital Staff Dress as Superheroes for Halloween Celebrations
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: Dressed as superheroes, hospital staff bring Halloween trick-or-treating to hospitalized kids
Hospital staff at Kaiser Permanente dressed as superheroes and other characters to celebrate Halloween with hospitalized children. Physicians, nurses, and even dogs in costumes led trick-or-treating through the Pediatrics Department, allowing kids to experience Halloween traditions despite their medical conditions. Four-year-old Leo Beltran, dressed as Captain America, expressed his love for candy, while his mother Brianna described the moment as emotionally rewarding. Staff member Rita emphasized the importance of festive activities, stating, 'We do this for them... to celebrate like every other child.' The event aimed to mimic normal Halloween experiences, ensuring hospitalized children could partake in the holiday. Brianna called the staff's efforts 'heartwarming and rewarding,' noting the significance of the celebration for her son. The initiative reflects the hospital's commitment to providing joy and normalcy during medical treatment.

item.title: Global citizens prepare emergency kits for crises
item.description:
Source: BBC News Original headline: Responsible or panicked? Meet the people around the world already preparing for crisis
Global citizens prepare emergency kits for crises. In Sweden, Andreas Wennerberg received a government booklet detailing crisis preparedness, stockpiling €200 in cash, 10 liters of water, and a crank radio. He admits he hasn't fully followed guidance but feels secure. In Maryland, Dan C, a parent, spent $6,000 on supplies including 150 gallons of water, solar panels, and medical kits, rotating food to prevent spoilage. Japan's Ayumi T updated her kit after a 2024 earthquake, keeping a rucksack with hygiene items and disposable toilets. Nicole Bonds in Georgia gradually accumulates supplies like batteries and first-aid kits. In the Netherlands, Michael Stuut stores 120 liters of water and a generator in his home, using an app to track food expiration. Dutch authorities recently urged 72 hours of supplies, a guideline also adopted by the UK. All emphasize preparedness as responsibility, not panic, to aid emergency services.

item.title: Flying cars require $300K and space, per Alef and Tesla
item.description:
Source: Business Insider Original headline: Flying cars are coming. You’ll need $300K and the space to fly it.
Alef Aeronautics and Tesla are developing flying cars, with Alef planning deliveries by next year and Tesla's Roadster with flight features starting in 2028. Alef's model costs $300,000 with a $150,000 deposit, while Tesla's Roadster requires a $250,000 deposit. CEO Jim Dukhovny said flying cars need dedicated takeoff and landing spaces, citing San Francisco's Market Street as unsuitable. University of California professor Alexandre Bayen noted regulatory, infrastructure, and public acceptance hurdles, calling mass transit use unrealistic for decades. Early use cases include remote areas and elite short commutes. Companies like Joby Aircraft and Archer Aviation are developing eVTOLs, but Dukhovny emphasized flying cars differ by driving on roads. Tesla did not comment on the request for comment.

item.title: 11-Year-Old Hospitalized After Chula Vista Chain-Reaction Crash
item.description:
Source: ABC 10News San Diego Original headline: 11-year-old remains hospitalized after Chula Vista chain-reaction crash
A chain-reaction crash on Fourth Avenue near Moss Street in Chula Vista injured a mother and her three children. Isabel Aguiar, driving her 9-year-old son, 11-year-old daughter Areli, and 15-year-old son to school, was involved in the collision around 8:30 a.m. Three vehicles were struck in the crash. Aguiar suffered fractures to her neck and spine, along with injuries to her pelvis, ribs, elbow, foot, and lung, and developed a blood clot in her knee. Her 9-year-old son also sustained similar injuries and a head injury. Areli, the 11-year-old, suffered the most severe injuries, including a life-threatening head trauma, and remains in a medically induced coma. Doctors are slowly weaning her from sedation, but her prognosis is uncertain. Aguiar, who woke up in the hospital with no memory of the crash, stays at her daughter’s bedside, speaking to her in hopes she can hear. A GoFundMe campaign supports the family’s medical costs. Police confirmed no alcohol or drugs were involved, and the investigation continues. No arrests have been made. Witnesses are urged to contact the Chula Vista Police Department Traffic Bureau for information.
